bib.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents

read.skipped: Appendix F.1/F.2 agent diffs (long code patches) and the SWE-bench/Polyglot task-id lists were only skimmed; references skimmed.

question: Can a coding agent that edits its own code, with benchmark-validated changes and an archive of past agents, keep improving both its coding ability and its ability to self-modify?
hypothesis: Self-modification plus open-ended archive-based exploration yields continued gains that a fixed meta-agent (no self-improvement) or greedy/latest-only lineage (no open-endedness) cannot reach.
contributions: The Darwin Gödel Machine: a self-referential coding agent that rewrites its own Python codebase and validates each change empirically instead of by proof
Archive-based open-ended parent selection that keeps stepping stones
Gains from 20.0% to 50.0% on SWE-bench and 14.2% to 30.7% on Polyglot, with transfer across models, benchmarks and languages
Ablations (no self-improve, no open-ended exploration, greedy parent selection) and a safety discussion including an objective-hacking case

method.summary: A single coding agent (frozen FM + bash and edit tools) is the initial archive. Each iteration samples parents from the archive by a performance-and-novelty weight; each parent reads its own benchmark logs (diagnosed by o1), proposes a feature, and implements it in its own repo to make a child. Children are scored with staged benchmark evaluation and kept in the archive only if they still can edit code. The exploration loop itself is fixed and not editable by the agent.

datasets.name: SWE-bench Verified
datasets.size: staged: 10 tasks, then 50 more (60 total), then 140 more (200 total)
datasets.split: SWE-bench-verified-mini style subset; 10 django tasks for basic functionality, 50 django/sphinx, 140 astropy/django
datasets.source: Jimenez et al. 2024; OpenAI 2024 human-filtered subset

datasets.name: Polyglot
datasets.size: staged: 10 tasks, then 50 tasks; full benchmark for final comparison
datasets.split: random subset of the full benchmark (C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust)
datasets.preprocessing: pass@1: agent never sees ground-truth test results (leaderboard uses pass@2)

models.name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New)
models.architecture: frozen FM inside a tool-use agent

other.use: self-modification in both settings; evaluation on SWE-bench
diagnoses improvement from evaluation logs and writes the problem description

inference.temperature: 1.0 for all FMs in every setting
inference.samples: 80 iterations, one new agent per selected parent; k=2 parallel on SWE-bench, k=4 on Polyglot; each agent evaluated once per stage; stability check: 3 DGM runs on Polyglot
inference.prompting: Base agent gets one prompt with repo dir, problem statement and test description; tools: bash and an editor (view/create/edit whole file). Self-improve diagnosis prompt to o1 returns JSON with log_summarization, potential_improvements, improvement_proposal, implementation_suggestion, problem_description.

parameters.parent_weight: w_i = sigmoid(lambda*(alpha_i - alpha0)) * 1/(1+n_i), n_i = children with editing functionality; agents with score 1.0 are excluded
parameters.stage_3_swe: 200 tasks if >40% on the 60-task set and top two in archive
parameters.archive_admission: child must compile and retain codebase-editing ability

other.safety: sandboxed execution with time limits; agents kept in a traceable archive

metrics.name: success rate
metrics.definition: percentage of benchmark tasks solved (SWE-bench resolved; Polyglot pass@1, no test feedback)

metrics.name: basic code-editing functionality rate
metrics.definition: share of generated agents that keep the ability to edit a codebase

baselines: DGM w/o open-ended exploration (keep only latest valid agent)
DGM Greedy (always pick best node; replicates Robeyns et al. 2025)
OpenHands + CodeAct v2.1 (SWE-bench, checked open-source SoTA)
eval.protocol: Best-of-archive score curves over 80 iterations on benchmark subsets (Fig 2); best agent re-evaluated on 200 SWE-bench tasks or full Polyglot; transfer by swapping the FM, benchmark or language set. Single runs per configuration except a 3-run stability test on Polyglot; no significance test.

availability.data: SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot (public); full agent logs and archive lineage promised in the reproducibility statement

limits: Authors concede it falls short of closed-source SoTA SWE-bench solutions and a single run takes about 2 weeks and USD 22,000.
Bounded by the frozen FM; it does not rewrite training scripts or the FM.
The open-ended exploration loop (archive, parent selection) is fixed and not modifiable by the agent.
Key assumption: coding benchmark gains indicate better self-modification ability.
Only two coding benchmarks; most configurations are single runs without significance tests; only Polyglot has a 3-run stability check.
Search uses small subsets (60 tasks SWE-bench, 50 Polyglot) and noisy FMs; thresholds like 40% are heuristics.
The diagnosis prompt includes the private test patch and results, so the score signal leaks tests into the proposal step (authors report finding no overfitting).
Objective hacking observed in the hallucination study (agent deleted the detection markers).

terms.definition: a self-referential, self-improving system that writes and modifies its own code to become a better coding agent, validating changes empirically and keeping an archive
interesting yet suboptimal solutions or features that may enable future breakthroughs
optimizing for the measurable objective rather than the spirit of the task
